claims.answer: Web app (app.im.codes or self-hosted, usable on phones), iOS/iPad/Apple Watch apps via the App Store, Android apps (APK/AAB), Telegram/Discord/Feishu bots, and the imcodes CLI daemon on macOS and Linux (Windows experimental via ConPTY); Windows/macOS/Linux Controlled Nodes provide remote desktop (Windows) from browser or phone. retention.answer: No retention period is stated: data stays until the user deletes it (export or delete at any time); hosted account deletion permanently removes all stored data, and a self-hosted server's data lives until its operator removes it.

training.answer: Unknown: the privacy page states no sale, sharing or transfer to third parties but does not address training use; model traffic is governed by each agent provider's terms.

telemetry_disclosure.answer: Partial: the privacy page states no third-party analytics or tracking cookies and that relayed data 'is not harvested or analyzed'; it does not describe the daemon's automatic token-usage upload, which the source at 799fa96 performs and the bound server aggregates into usage summaries.

telemetry_defaults.answer: On by default when bound to the vendor-hosted app.im.codes: at source revision 799fa96 (committed 2026-11-17 03:01 UTC; scope names release android-v1.1-b8442c5) the daemon's usage-sync worker POSTs token-usage facts (session name, provider, agent type, model, token counts, context window, cost) at startup and every 60 seconds to the server it is bound to, so evaluation users of app.im.codes send them to the vendor, while a self-hosted server keeps them with its operator. This conflicts with the privacy page's promise that relayed data is not harvested or analyzed; the code decides. A bounded search of the same revision found no third-party analytics or crash-reporting client: shared/memory-telemetry.ts and shared/timeline-delivery-telemetry.ts only feed in-process counters, X-Platform/X-App-Version headers are auth audit records on the sign-in server, and --disable-telemetry switches off the third-party Antigravity CLI's telemetry.

telemetry_controls.answer: No control: at 799fa96 the usage-sync worker starts whenever the daemon has server credentials, and no setting, flag or environment variable disables it; the only way to keep the facts away from the vendor is to bind to a self-hosted server. Optional cloud memory sync is a separate setting.

telemetry_off_switch.answer: No off switch: a bounded search of 799fa96 (usage-sync, usageSync, USAGE_SYNC and disable/enabled terms across src, shared, server and web) found no setting, flag or environment variable that stops the token-usage upload; it runs whenever the daemon is bound, and only binding to a self-hosted server instead of app.im.codes keeps the facts from the vendor.

consent_prompt.answer: None: at 799fa96 imcodes bind saves server credentials and restarts the daemon without asking anything or mentioning the usage upload, and the daemon starts the upload whenever credentials exist.

provider_separation.answer: Model requests are made by the agents the daemon runs on the user's machine (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen and others, through tmux or their SDKs) under each provider's terms; the IM.codes server only relays traffic between the user's devices and the daemon.

limitations: Hosted retention period, subprocessors and residency not documented.
training: The privacy page does not address training use.
claims.unknownReason: Hosted residency and subprocessors are business facts not stated; the privacy page does not address training use.

evidence.title: IM.codes source at 799fa96: bounded telemetry inspection
evidence.locator: shared/memory-telemetry.ts; shared/timeline-delivery-telemetry.ts; shared/metrics.ts lines 1-15; server/src/routes/auth.ts lines 96-115 (getAuthRequestMetadata, logAuthAudit); shared/agy-agent.ts line 70 and src/agent/agy-incognito-isolation.ts line 824; search terms posthog, segment, amplitude, mixpanel, sentry, aptabase, telemetry, DO_NOT_TRACK, google-analytics, gtag, firebase/analytics, opentelemetry, X-Platform, X-App-Version
evidence.finding: No third-party analytics or crash-reporting client sends data to the vendor. shared/memory-telemetry.ts and shared/timeline-delivery-telemetry.ts define label sets and counter names fed to shared/metrics.ts, an in-process, non-persisted Map in the user's own daemon and server. The X-Platform, X-App-Version and X-Bundle-Version request headers are written by server/src/routes/auth.ts into the audit_log table of whichever server the user signs in to (their self-hosted server or the hosted app.im.codes account service), as auth audit records rather than an analytics feed. shared/agy-agent.ts defines --disable-telemetry, which the daemon passes to the third-party Google Antigravity (agy) CLI to turn that tool's telemetry off. Other matches are audio amplitude fields and a DO_NOT_TRACK=1 value passed to child npm processes. This search covers analytics and crash-reporting clients only: separately, src/daemon/usage-sync-worker.ts uploads token-usage facts to the bound server, including the vendor-hosted app.im.codes (see tel-2611-usage-sync).

evidence.title: imcodes 799fa96 daemon usage-sync worker
evidence.locator: src/daemon/lifecycle.ts lines 1731 and 2812-2830 (startUsageSyncWorker); src/daemon/usage-sync-worker.ts (DEFAULT_USAGE_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS 60000, POST to /api/server/:id/token-usage/ingest); shared/usage-analytics.ts lines 172-189 (UsageFact); server/src/routes/token-usage.ts lines 30 and 123; README.md lines 311-316 (app.im.codes evaluation instance, imcodes bind). Search for usage-sync, usageSync, USAGE_SYNC and disable/enabled terms across src, shared, server and web.
evidence.finding: Whenever the daemon has server credentials (after imcodes bind), lifecycle.ts starts the usage-sync worker, which POSTs batches of token-usage facts (session name and kind, provider, agent type, model, input/cache/output/total tokens, context window, cost) at startup and every 60 seconds to /api/server/:serverId/token-usage/ingest on the bound server; the server stores them and serves the user's token-usage summary. The README offers the vendor-hosted app.im.codes for evaluation (imcodes bind https://app.im.codes/bind/<api-key>), so evaluation users send these facts to the vendor; a self-hosted server keeps them with its operator. The only gate is the presence of credentials; no setting, flag or environment variable disables the upload.

evidence.title: IM.codes Privacy Policy (last updated March 2026)
evidence.locator: Data Storage; What We Store; Data Ownership; Third-Party Sharing; Account Deletion; Cookies & Analytics
evidence.finding: Data is stored on the user's own server or on app.im.codes; 'We do not operate centralized data collection infrastructure.' Users can export or delete their data at any time; hosted account deletion permanently removes all stored data, and removing a self-hosted server removes its data. No retention period is given. 'We do not sell, share, or transfer your data to third parties. The server acts as a relay ... data passes through but is not harvested or analyzed.' No third-party analytics or tracking cookies. The page says nothing about model training or a consent prompt.

evidence.title: IM.codes README: architecture and self-hosting
evidence.locator: README.md lines 301 (daemon and agents) and 311-316 (app.im.codes evaluation instance)
evidence.finding: The daemon on the developer machine runs the agents through tmux or local SDKs and gateways (Claude Code SDK, Codex SDK, OpenClaw gateway, Qwen); the server only relays connections between the user's devices and the daemon. The shared app.im.codes instance is for testing only, and self-hosting is strongly recommended.

evidence.title: IM.codes bind flow and usage-sync start
evidence.locator: src/bind/bind-flow.ts (all 430 lines: imcodes bind, credential save, daemon restart and service install); src/daemon/lifecycle.ts lines 2812-2830 (startUsageSyncWorker); search of src/bind and src/cli.ts for consent, confirm, prompt, readline and usage
evidence.finding: imcodes bind <url> registers the device, saves the server credentials and restarts or installs the daemon, printing only binding and service status; it asks no question and does not mention the token-usage upload. startUsageSyncWorker starts the upload whenever workerUrl, serverId and token are present, with no consent check.
